## _**I made a transfer of $500,000 to the Abubakars through my company, China Castle Investments Ltd, in early 2003 – Leno Adesanya**_

YOU DO NOT NEED to look further for the Abubakars referred to above by Leno Laitan ‘Mambilla’ Adesanya, the man who wanted to reap where he did not sow. Adesanya was talking about the Atiku Abubakar family in his witness statement to the International Chamber of Commerce Arbitration Tribunal in Paris, France, which last week threw out his petition against Nigeria.

Adesanya whose first name Leno creates the impression that he is a foreigner had gone to the tribunal to seek $2.35 billion compensation as well as $400 million settlement fee for what he called the failed Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in Taraba State. He claimed that his firm, Sunrise Power and Transmission Company, was awarded the contract for the 3,960Mw Mambilla power project in 2003. The tribunal found that there was no such contract because it never got the necessary presidential approval.

Adesanya’s failure to meet this condition-precedent was fatal to his claim, and he and his collaborators like Atiku and former Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Abubakar Malami, who was expected to defend the national interest as Nigeria’s chief law officer, but failed to do so, paid dearly for it. Rather than watch out for Nigeria’s interest, Malami was at every turn pushing Adesanya’s case and piling pressure on the late President Muhammadu Buhari to sign off on it.

Buhari refused and Adesanya blew his cool. The so-called high networth businessman whose firm Sunrise, according to the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) books, had only N1,000,000 in total declared net assets at the time of the said contract, then rushed to the tribunal, without giving the matter a second thought. If he had paused and caught his breath, he would not have taken that route. But then, such ‘businessmen’ are not known to be rational. They act on impulse believing that what money cannot buy, more money will buy.

“At the time they received the ‘award’, the financial position of the company was N318,685 on 3rd December 2004 and N270,370 as of 31st December 2005”, Mallam Garba Shehu, Buhari’s media aide, said last weekend. Shehu should know as he attended the tribunal’s sitting in January last year. Sunrise’s financial standing as at 2004/2005 did not show that it is a firm with the capcaity to execute a contract as huge as the Mambilla project. How can a firm with only a few thousands in its account undertake a multi billion dollars power project?

It is only in our country that such a firm will attempt to do that, with the backing of insiders who are only interested in what they will gain. The craze for fast bucks by many in public office is our greatest undoing as a nation. What did Atiku’s wife, Jennifer, do for Leno Adesanya to wire her $500,000? Was it a gift or payment for services rendered? Adesanya could not explain why he sent her the money. Yet, he swore on oath to say the truth and nothing but the truth. When the chips were down, he could not reveal the whole truth.

He knew that going beyond saying that he gave Jennifer $500,000 would be damaging to her husband, so he withheld further disclosure. The tribunal itself was stunned by the huge monetary offer, which it knew, could not have been given without strings attached. It did all it could to unravel the truth, but Adesanya declined to make full disclosure. He merely described it as a foreign-exchange transaction for Atiku. Is Adesanya also a moneychanger?
